problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(5,3,0).$

activity_context.topic_title: The Parametric Equations of a Line

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068356/assets/99504eaa41497c5be9baa7c860c97ab5ba5c858609e47ad347f24ec9b8ffc940.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(3,6,8)$ and $Q(-2,-5,4).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -11 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -11 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5t \\ -11t \\ -4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3-5t \\ 6-11t \\ 8-4t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-5t \\ y=6-11t \\ z=8-4t\end{aligned}
$$
